22496-the-settlers-in-canada.description: A book by Captain Marryat. se new settlers were obliged to go into or toward Upper Canada, where, although the land was better, the distance from Quebec and Montreal, and other populous parts, was much greater, and they were left almost wholly to their own resources, and almost without protection.

arxiv-1610-05569.title: Transverse momentum and multiplicity fluctuations in Ar+Sc collisions at the CERN SPS from NA61/SHINE Thanks: Presented at Critical Point and Onset of Deconfinement 2016, Wroclaw, Poland, May 30th - June 4th, 2016
arxiv-1610-05569.creator: Evgeny Andronov for the NA61/SHINE Collaboration
arxiv-1610-05569.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Evgeny Andronov for the NA61/SHINE Collaboration. The NA61/SHINE experiment aims to discover the critical point of strongly interacting matter and study the properties of the onset of deconfinement. For these goals a scan of the two dimensional phase diagram ( T T - μ B \mu_{B} ) is being performed at the SPS by measurements of hadron production in proton-proton, proton-nucleus and nucleus-nucleus interactions as a function of collision energy and system size.

arxiv-2109-01936.title: Influence of NaMo App on Twitter
arxiv-2109-01936.creator: Shreya Sharma, Samiya Caur, Hitkul, Ponnurangam Kumaraguru
arxiv-2109-01936.description: Abstract . Social media plays a crucial role in today’s society. It results in paradigm changes in how people relate and communicate, convey and exchange ideas. Moreover, social media has evolved into critical knowledge networks for consumers and also affects decision-making.

arxiv-2208-11593.description: Abstract . For Lebesgue generic ( x 1 , x 2 ) ∈ ℝ 2 ({x}_{1},x_{2})\in\mathbb{R}^{2} , we investigate the distribution of small values of products q ⋅ ‖ q ​ x 1 ‖ ⋅ ‖ q ​ x 2 ‖ q\cdot\|qx_{1}\|\cdot\|qx_{2}\| with q ∈ ℕ q\in\mathbb{N} , where ∥ ⋅ ∥ \|\cdot\| denotes the distance to the closest integer.

arxiv-2301-10860.title: Skeleton coupling: a novel interlayer mapping of community evolution in temporal networks
arxiv-2301-10860.creator: Bengier Ülgen Kilic, Sarah Feldt Muldoon
arxiv-2301-10860.description: Abstract Abstract Dynamic community detection (DCD) in temporal networks is a complicated task that involves the selection of a method and its associated hyperparameters. How to choose the most appropriate method generally depends on the type of network being analyzed and the specific properties of the data that define the network.

arxiv-2306-17794.title: Vision Through the Veil: Differential Privacy in Federated Learning for Medical Image Classification
arxiv-2306-17794.creator: Kishore Babu Nampalle, Pradeep Singh
arxiv-2306-17794.description: Abstract The proliferation of deep learning applications in healthcare calls for data aggregation across various institutions, a practice often associated with significant privacy concerns. This concern intensifies in medical image analysis, where privacy-preserving mechanisms are paramount due to the data being sensitive in nature. Federated learning, which enables cooperative model training without direct data exchange, presents a promising solution.

arxiv-2405-01102.title: Less is More: on the Over-Globalizing Problem in Graph Transformers
arxiv-2405-01102.creator: Yujie Xing, Xiao Wang, Yibo Li, Hai Huang, Chuan Shi
arxiv-2405-01102.description: Abstract Graph Transformer, due to its global attention mechanism, has emerged as a new tool in dealing with graph-structured data. It is well recognized that the global attention mechanism considers a wider receptive field in a fully connected graph, leading many to believe that useful information can be extracted from all the nodes.

arxiv-2406-08649.title: MOTI 𝒱 ​ ℰ \mathcal{V}\mathcal{E} : A Drug-Target Interaction Graph For Inductive Link Prediction
arxiv-2406-08649.creator: John Arevalo, Ellen SuAnne E. CarpenterShantanu SinghBroad Institute of MIT and Harvard {jarevalo, suellen, anne, shantanu}@broadinstitute.org
arxiv-2406-08649.description: Abstract Drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction is crucial for identifying new therapeutics and detecting mechanisms of action. While structure-based methods accurately model physical interactions between a drug and its protein target, cell-based assays such as Cell Painting can better capture complex DTI interactions.

arxiv-2407-14704.title: Reactor-based Search for Axion-Like Particles using CsI(Tl) Detector Journal: arxiv.org
arxiv-2407-14704.creator: S. Sahoo, S. Verma, M. Mirzakhani, N. Mishra, A. Thompson, S. Maludze, R. Mahapatra, M. Platt
arxiv-2407-14704.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by S. Sahoo, S. Verma, M. Mirzakhani, N. Mishra, A. Thompson, S. Maludze, R. Mahapatra, M. Platt. Null results for WIMP dark matter have led to increased interest in exploring other dark matter candidates, such as Axions and Axion-Like Particles (ALPs), which also helps in answering the strong CP problem. This experiment achieved a sub-100 DRU (differential-rate-unit, expressed in counts/keV/kg/day) background in the MeV region of interest by employing a combination of active and passive veto techniques.

arxiv-2409-01999.title: Characterisation of the Atmosphere in Very High Energy Gamma-Astronomy for Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes
arxiv-2409-01999.creator: Dijana Dominis Prester *, Jan Ebr, Markus Gaug, Alexander Hahn, Ana Babić \orcidJ, Jiří Eliášek \orcidH, Petr Janeček, Sergey Karpov \orcidI, Marta Kolarek \orcidK, Marina Manganaro * \orcidG, Razmik Mirzoyan
arxiv-2409-01999.description: Abstract Ground-based observations of Very High Energy (VHE) gamma rays from extreme astrophysical sources are significantly influenced by atmospheric conditions. This is due to the atmosphere being an integral part of the detector when utilizing Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs).

arxiv-2409-06877.title: Positive equilibria in mass action networks: geometry and bounds
arxiv-2409-06877.creator: Murad Banaji 1 and Elisenda Feliu 2
arxiv-2409-06877.description: Abstract . Any mass action network gives rise to a parameterised family of polynomial equations whose positive solutions are the positive equilibria of the network. Here, we consider alternative systems of equations, whose solutions are in smooth, one-to-one correspondence with positive equilibria of the network, and capture degeneracy or nondegeneracy of the corresponding equilibria.

arxiv-2410-05768.title: My view on and experience with Grothendieck’s anabelian geometry
arxiv-2410-05768.creator: Mohamed Saïdi
arxiv-2410-05768.description: Abstract This paper is based on the author’s talk at the Grothendieck conference at Chapman university on 26-05-2022. It is not a survey of anabelian geometry but rather exposes some of the personal views and experiences of the author with the topic. §0. Introduction Alexander Grothendieck (1928-2014) was undoubtedly one of the greatest mathematician of all times.

arxiv-2505-06098.title: Discretized Approximate Ancestral Sampling
arxiv-2505-06098.creator: Alfredo De la Fuente, Saurabh Singh, Jona Ballé
arxiv-2505-06098.description: Abstract The Fourier Basis Density Model (FBM) [ 1 ] was recently introduced as a flexible probability model for band-limited distributions, i.e. ones which are smooth in the sense of having a characteristic function with limited support around the origin.

arxiv-2505-22399.title: Learning to Pursue AC Optimal Power Flow Solutions with Feasibility Guarantees
arxiv-2505-22399.creator: Damola Ajeyemi, Yiting Chen, Antonin Colot, Jorge Cortés, Emiliano Dall’Anese
arxiv-2505-22399.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Damola Ajeyemi, Yiting Chen, Antonin Colot, Jorge Cortés, Emiliano Dall’Anese. This paper focuses on an AC optimal power flow (OPF) problem for distribution feeders equipped with controllable distributed energy resources (DERs). We consider a solution method that is based on a continuous approximation of the projected gradient flow – referred to as the safe gradient flow – that incorporates voltage and current information obtained either through real-time measurements or power flow computations. These two setups enable both feedback-based online and offline implementations.

arxiv-2512-05183.title: Quantum compilation framework for data loading
arxiv-2512-05183.creator: Guillermo Alonso-Linaje, Utkarsh Azad, Jay Soni, Jarrett Smalley, Leigh Lapworth, Juan Miguel Arrazola
arxiv-2512-05183.description: Abstract Efficient encoding of classical data into quantum circuits is a critical challenge that directly impacts the scalability of quantum algorithms. In this work, we present an automated compilation framework for resource-aware quantum data loading tailored to a given input vector and target error tolerance.

arxiv-2601-09562.title: MM-BRIGHT: A Multi-Task Multimodal Benchmark for Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval
arxiv-2601-09562.creator: Abdelrahman Abdallah, Mohamed Darwish Mounis, Mahmoud Abdalla, Mahmoud SalahEldin Kasem, Mostafa Farouk Senussi, Mohamed Mahmoud, Mohammed Ali, Adam Jatowt, Hyun-Soo Kang, [0.5em] University of Innsbruck, [0.3em] Equal contribution
arxiv-2601-09562.description: Abstract Existing retrieval benchmarks primarily consist of text-based queries where keyword or semantic matching is usually sufficient. Many real-world queries contain multimodal elements, particularly, images such as diagrams, charts, and screenshots that require intensive reasoning to identify relevant documents. To address this gap, we introduce MM-BRIGHT , the first multimodal benchmark for reasoning-intensive retrieval.

pmc-10510115.creator: Eleojo Oluwaseun Abubakar, Niall Cunningham
pmc-10510115.description: BackgroundPrecise geographical targeting is well recognised as an indispensable intervention strategy for achieving many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). pmc-12672721.description: Long COVID affects multiple body systems, with the respiratory system being particularly vulnerable. This study aimed to analyze the lung ventilatory function and diffusion capacity of patients with severe SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia during a 24-month follow-up course. Ventilatory function and lung diffusion capacity were assessed 6, 12, 18, and 24 months after hospital discharge.

pmc-13118941.title: Interfacial and Bulk Properties of Volatile Amphiphiles and Sodium Dodecyl Sulfate Mixtures
pmc-13118941.creator: Ralitsa Uzunova, Rumyana Stanimirova, Krassimir Danov
pmc-13118941.description: Volatile amphiphiles and surfactant mixtures have gained wide applications in diverse areas of industry, cosmetics, and medicine. The surface tension isotherms, measured at different solute ratios, and data processing, using appropriate theoretical models, provide quantitative information on their bulk and interfacial properties.

pmc-13188782.title: Co-designing a psychoeducational intervention for FCs of institutionalized older adults : a participatory double diamond approach
pmc-13188782.creator: Souad Meziane-Damnée, Anne-Sophie Rigaud, Catherine Bayle, Matthieu Piccoli, Lauriane Blavette, Sébastien Dacunha, Hermine Lenoir, Maribel Pino
pmc-13188782.description: BackgroundThe transition of a relative with dementia into long-term care is a critical and emotionally charged period for family caregivers, often marked by guilt, loss of role, and strained relationships with care teams. While psychosocial interventions can mitigate these challenges, few are co-designed with both caregivers and professionals to ensure contextual relevance.

pmc-13189727.title: Feature-based clustering of hemoglobin trajectories and subsequent risk of end-stage kidney disease in stages 3–4 CKD: a landmark analysis
pmc-13189727.creator: Na Sun, Nan Hu, Jinping Li, Xichao Wang, Wenyu Zhang, Shunya Uchida, Yingying Han, Wenxiu Chang
pmc-13189727.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAnemia and protein-energy wasting (PEW) are common complications in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and are associated with disease progression. However, the prognostic significance of longitudinal hemoglobin (Hb) trajectory patterns, particularly in the context of nutritional status, remains unclear.

pmc-13606918.title: Expression and Immunogenic Application of Recombinant DENV-2 rprM Protein for the Non-Invasive Detection of Salivary IgA Antibodies
pmc-13606918.creator: Julio García-Cordero, Luis Alberto Sánchez-Vargas, Rosendo Luria-Pérez, Héctor Vivanco-Cid, Leticia Cedillo-Barrón, Jazmín García-Machorro, Gabriela Mellado-Sánchez
pmc-13606918.description: Dengue virus (DENV) serotypes 1–4 cause dengue, a major re-emerging disease in tropical and subtropical regions. This study evaluated the antigenicity of a recombinant DENV-2 premembrane protein (rprM-DENV-2) and its ability to detect anti-DENV human IgA antibodies. The rprM-DENV-2 protein was expressed in Escherichia coli, purified, and assessed for immunogenicity and antigenicity.
